title: Measures to Develop Baseline Artificial Intelligence Literacy of Students
what_it_is: Measures to Develop Baseline Artificial Intelligence Literacy of Students

sections.label: AI literacy and coding questions
sections.summary: Questions ask about AI literacy programmes, AI coding plans, launch timing, and whether teachers or third parties run them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what other programmes beyond the artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled tools on Singapore Student Learning Space will be put in place to develop baseline AI literacy of students; (b) whether there are plans to launch AI coding programmes in the curriculum; (c) if so, when will such programmes be targeted to be launched; and (d) whether such programmes will be run by teachers or third party service providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) how many students have applied to join the Artificial Intelligence Student Outreach Programme; (b) what is the respective percentage of applicants who are from (i) secondary schools (ii) polytechnics (iii) Integrated Programme schools and (iv) junior colleges; and (c) whether there are plans to increase the take-up rate of the programme.

sections.label: AI programme applicant breakdown
sections.summary: In 2023, close to 17,000 students applied, with 52% secondary, 11% polytechnic, 11% IP, 3% junior college, and 23% others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In 2023, close to 17,000 students applied to join the programme, with the breakdown of applicants as follows: (a) 11% from the polytechnics; (b) 52% from the secondary schools; (c) 11% from the IP schools; and (d) 3% from the junior colleges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Students from the autonomous universities and the Institute of Technical Education make up the remaining 23% of applicants.

sections.label: SkillsFuture AI courses for adults
sections.summary: Working adults can take AI-related SkillsFuture courses to become smart and secure AI users in their industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Beyond our schools and IHLs, working adults can take up AI-related SkillsFuture courses to become smart and secure users of AI in their respective industries.

sections.label: AI adaptive learning for mathematics
sections.summary: An AI-enabled adaptive learning system for mathematics has been available on the Singapore Student Learning Space for Primary 5 topics since 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: At another level, we also use an AI-enabled adaptive learning system (ALS) for mathematics that has been made available through our Singapore Student Learning Space (SLS) for Primary 5-level topics since 2023, with more topics to be progressively rolled out in the next two years.

sections.label: Habits beyond school premises
sections.summary: The hope is that these habits apply beyond school premises and throughout students' lives, and Mr Ong's suggestion will be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Hopefully, these habits apply to them not just within the school premises, but also, throughout their lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will take into account Mr Ong's suggestion.

sections.label: AI refining designs and prompts
sections.summary: With AI, designs can be refined in perhaps half the time, and students learnt to sharpen the prompts needed to start the process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, with AI, they can refine the designs very quickly – using, perhaps, half the time that they used to, using the previous method.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But the second thing that they have also learnt and very importantly, is how to sharpen – as the Member said – the prompt required in order to start the whole process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If the prompts are not well-crafted, then, you could be doing things very fast, but not necessarily down the correct path.

sections.label: Ethical AI use importance
sections.summary: Learning to use AI is important, but learning to use AI ethically is even more important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, we certainly agree that learning to use AI is important, but learning to use AI ethically is even more important.

sections.label: Students critiquing AI product
sections.summary: Teachers wanted students to know the AI's sources and critique the AI product, understanding its upside, downside and potential biases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: After they crafted the essay, the teachers wanted the students to: first, know the sources of information that the AI draws upon; then, the teachers encouraged the students to critique the AI product so that they can understand the upside and the downside of the product and also, the potential biases that that algorithm has generated.

sections.label: PISA logical thinking results
sections.summary: In recent PISA results, students did well in logical thinking and computational thinking traits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Even in the recent Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) results, we are glad that our students have done well in terms of their ability to think logically and to exhibit traits of computational thinking.

sections.label: Opportunities across socio-economic backgrounds
sections.summary: The Member asked whether the described opportunities are evenly available to students across households of diverse socio-economic backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can the Minister assure us that the opportunities he described in his answer are evenly available for students across households of diverse social economic backgrounds?

sections.label: Home learning access and digital divide
sections.summary: MOE ensured students have laptops, tablets, computers and bandwidth at home, running online and offline systems to avoid a digital divide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, we made sure that even if the students do not come to school, they have access to laptops, tablets and computers so that they can learn at home and we even made sure that they have access to the bandwidth necessary to support the working of this laptop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, our teachers actually run two systems in parallel whereby we have online access and also offline, back-in-the-school access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is MOE's commitment to make sure that, through the use of technology, we do not end up with a digital divide but, instead, we use technology to democratise the access to the best material available to all students.

sections.label: Working with MCI and Ministries
sections.summary: The answer is yes, and they are working closely with MCI and other Ministries to do this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The answer is yes, we are working closely with MCI and other Ministries to do this.

sections.label: Trust in information, MOE MCI
sections.summary: The speaker says reasoned debate and elections require trustworthy information, and that MOE and MCI will work with stakeholders to develop a framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We cannot have reasoned debate, elections and so forth, if we cannot trust the information that we are accessing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, I think this requires a whole-of-nation effort and, definitely, MOE and MCI will be working closely with all our stakeholders to develop the framework that the Member suggested.
